summary: The agent implemented nearly all map/iterable entry-mapping behavior and passed all 3,641 baseline tests plus 30 of 32 new tests, but incorrectly allowed Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map mapping methods to compile.
quick_failure_summary: Map/Stream cross-container methods compile even though the feature is limited to maps with iterables or arrays.

details.reasoning: The implementation broadly relaxed MethodRetrievalProcessor validation whenever either side was a Map. Because the existing predicate groups Stream and Iterable types, these conditions also exempted Stream-to-Map and Map-to-Stream signatures. The hidden boundary test therefore observed successful compilation where the existing diagnostics should have been emitted. The correct approach limits the exceptions to parameterType.isIterableType() with a map result and a map parameter with resultType.isIterableType(), preserving the separate stream mapping family.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's focused and adjacent tests did not include a Map/Stream boundary case, despite inspecting the separate StreamMappingMethod path and existing erroneous stream tests. Otherwise the implementation was substantial and passed every functional entry-mapping test.

justification.issue_description: The method-retrieval exceptions for the new feature were widened to all stream-or-iterable types, unintentionally enabling Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map mappings.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly scopes support to an 'iterable or array result' and an 'iterable or array source'; java.util.stream.Stream is neither Iterable nor an array. The visible codebase separately classifies stream mappings in SourceMethod.isStreamMapping() and implements them through StreamMappingMethod. Existing ErroneousStreamMappingTest coverage also preserves diagnostics between streams and unsupported non-stream/non-iterable types. In the agent patch, MethodRetrievalProcessor changes `!resultType.isIterableOrStreamType()` to also allow any map result and changes the reverse check to allow any map parameter, thereby exempting streams as well as iterables.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented-test mismatch: the supported source and result families were stated in the prompt, Stream is a distinct Java type, and both production structure and existing tests made the stream boundary reasonably foreseeable. The implementation works for the requested map/iterable and map/array cases but misses this explicit scope boundary.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is a fair compiler-modeling change spanning method classification, element selection, code generation, abstract Map.Entry construction, qualifiers, lower bounds, and container subtypes. The failing boundary is reasonably implied by the explicit iterable/array scope and the repository's separate stream-mapping architecture. The verifier deterministically checks both compilers and reports the same boundary failure twice.

evidence: The trajectory shows successful processor compilation, focused tests, 102 adjacent tests, checkstyle, and git diff validation.
The verifier completed normally: all 3,641 baseline tests passed, and the new suite reached assertions with 30 passes and two deterministic expected-compilation failures.
An early `rg`-not-found result and permission warnings from an overly broad `find ..` were immediately worked around with grep/find under `/app` and did not materially divert or block implementation.
Both new failures directly exercise the agent-modified method-retrieval logic rather than shared bootstrap, dependency, runtime, or test-harness setup.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; method validation was broadened beyond the requested iterable/array mapping families.
